accepted_recoveries: Lower the JVM maximum heap to the benchmark's known-safe value while retaining non-heap headroom.
Raise the container memory request and limit to the benchmark's known-safe values after proving namespace and node capacity.
forbidden_actions: Do not disable the container memory limit.
Do not change node or kernel OOM policy.
Do not treat exit code 137 alone as proof of heap OOM without cgroup and JVM evidence.
incident.injected_fault: The pricing JVM starts with -Xmx512m inside a container limited to 256Mi, causing cgroup OOM termination with exit code 137 under the benchmark load.
observable_signals: Pricing pods restart repeatedly and show Last State OOMKilled with exit code 137.
Container memory working set approaches the 256Mi limit before termination.
Node memory remains healthy, localizing pressure to the container limit.
preconditions: The pricing image and benchmark dataset are unchanged from the healthy fixture.
The namespace and nodes can accommodate the known-safe memory profile.
No node-level memory pressure condition is active.
required_evidence: Capture container last state, reason, exit code, and restart count.
Capture the JVM heap flags and container memory request and limit.
Capture container and node memory telemetry around a failure.
Run the benchmark load through all post-recovery SLO windows.
incident.title: Java heap OOM Exit 137

constraints: Capture last-state reason, exit code, and restart count before concluding the failure mode.
Capture JVM heap flags and the container memory request and limit.
Correlate container memory telemetry around a failure with node memory health.
Do not infer heap OOM from exit code 137 alone; require cgroup and JVM evidence.
Do not disable the container memory limit.
Do not change node or kernel OOM policy.
Any capacity-based recovery path requires proof of namespace and node capacity.
Recovery validation requires benchmark load across 3 consecutive SLO windows, each with HTTP 5xx rate below 0.001 and p95 latency below 200 ms.
Keep the pricing image and benchmark dataset unchanged when validating the incident boundary.
payload.impact: pricing-api pods repeatedly restart under benchmark load after container-scoped cgroup OOM termination; memory working set reaches the 256Mi limit while node memory remains healthy. Scope is limited to proofix-case-07/pricing-api and does not indicate node-level memory pressure. Exit code 137 is corroborative only and must be paired with OOMKilled last state, cgroup telemetry, and JVM/container configuration evidence.

hypotheses.cause: The JVM is being terminated by its container cgroup because the 256Mi memory limit cannot safely contain a JVM configured with -Xmx512m plus metaspace, code cache, thread stacks, and other non-heap memory.
contradicts: No raw cgroup memory.events data, JVM native-memory data, or timestamped container telemetry is included; -Xmx is a ceiling and exit 137 alone would not prove this cause.
supports: kubectl/get/pods#4b7e57c5ef49: pricing-api lastState is OOMKilled with exitCode 137 and restartCount 2.
kubectl/get/pods#4b7e57c5ef49: JVM arguments specify -Xmx512m, MaxMetaspaceSize=64m, and ReservedCodeCacheSize=32m while the container limit is 256Mi.
kubectl/get/deployments#79e3a971ed52: the invalid heap and container-limit combination is in the Deployment template, so it persists across restarts.
incident.observable_signals[1]: container working set approaches the 256Mi limit before termination.
kubectl/get/nodes#e97bca0d4ba1: vm-4 reports MemoryPressure=False and approximately 16Gi allocatable memory, localizing the failure to the container.

hypotheses.cause: The JVM reaches a Java heap OutOfMemoryError and exits itself because -XX:+ExitOnOutOfMemoryError is enabled, rather than being killed externally by the cgroup.
contradicts: kubectl/get/pods#4b7e57c5ef49 records reason OOMKilled and exitCode 137, which is more consistent with an external SIGKILL than an orderly JVM ExitOnOutOfMemoryError termination.
No Java heap-space OutOfMemoryError, heap dump, or JVM fatal-error evidence is supplied.
The 512m heap ceiling exceeds the entire 256Mi cgroup budget before accounting for non-heap memory.

kubectl/get/pods#4b7e57c5ef49: the configured heap maximum is large enough for heap exhaustion under load.

contradicts: Readiness-probe failures remove endpoints but do not restart containers.
The recorded last state is OOMKilled with exit code 137, not a probe-driven termination.

payload.rationale: The container was OOMKilled with exit code 137 and restarted twice while its JVM reported a roughly 495Mi maximum heap inside a 256Mi memory limit. Node MemoryPressure is false. Patch only the Deployment's JVM maximum heap to 128Mi, preserving the memory limit and leaving headroom for metaspace, code cache, thread stacks, and native memory. This is the smallest persistent, reversible remediation and does not modify or delete persistent data.
payload.rollback_trigger: Roll back if the replacement pod cannot become Ready, shows a new OOMKilled/restart event, or any of the 3 required benchmark windows has HTTP 5xx rate at or above 0.001 or p95 latency at or above 200 ms.

success_criteria.description: The replacement pod becomes Ready and remains Ready with no new OOMKilled termination or restart-count increase while benchmark load runs through 3 consecutive SLO windows; each window has HTTP 5xx rate below 0.001 and p95 latency below 200 ms.
